Bloem Zoo Crisis

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Animals at the Bloemfontein zoo left to die as the zoo's doors are closed.

Unique Selling Point:
In Feb/March 2019 Carte Blanche looked at the state of zoos around the country and the Bloemfontein Zoo was highlighted as an old fashioned zoo that provides very little educational value and poses a threat to the welfare of the animals. We saw barren, dirty enclosures where animals have very little stimulation and are surrounded by their own waste. Ponds and pools were dirty. The zoo was generally unkept. Then on 17 December 2019 the SPCA together with Free State Department: Economic, Small Business Development, Tourism and Environmental Affairs (DESTEA) closed the zoo down. The conditions had deteriorated to such an extent that the Manguang Municipality was ordered to move the animals and shut down the facility. The SPCA vowed to do regular inspections to check on the welfare of the animals. But by end Feb 2020 animals were dying from hunger and SPCA inspectors were greeted by a horrific scene.

Summary:
The Manguang Municipality of Bloemfontein has been adamant that the city's zoo delivers a positive contribution to the community. In the beginning of 2019 they claimed to have adequate capacity in terms of people and funding to keep the zoo running without hiccups - even though there had been public outcries about the state of the animals in the past. By the end of 2019, the municipality admitted that they do not have the necessary resources to keep the facility running and DESTEA stepped in. The zoo was closed down, and the animals were to be relocated to other state facilities. But this never happened and by March 2020 animals were dying. At the moment animals are being moved to other facilities by DESTEA, but there is concern that because it is now an emergency, animals are sent to all kinds of facilities, even private farms where hunting is allowed. So the question is, will these state assets simply be discarded?

There are also questions around the SPCA's conduct. On 7 Feb 2020 they issued a statement saying that the animals are fine.. Two weeks later animals are dying, buffalo are so sick that they're losing their hair, and many anilas are limping and listless. They were supposed to check regularly. What happened?



Further information:
Manguang Municipality spokesperson Qondile Khedama acknowledged on Friday that there had been a myriad of issues at the zoo that the municipality had been working towards resolving. He said representatives had visited the zoo recently to assess the situation and condition of the animals. “Among other issues we have noted a serious lack of, or insufficient resources but an urgent meeting has since been called for an engagement with various stakeholders,” he said.

The Bloemfontein Zoo has been in the news as early as 2012 about the conditions of enclosures and the state of animals.

There are additional allegations that the property where the zoo is situated is earmarked for development and is part of an ongoing property war in the city.

Accommodation for Crew in Bloemfontein.
Petrol for drive to and from Bloemfontein.

Bloem Zoo Closure 2020 SCRIPT


V/O
Scenes from Bloemfontein Zoo in February 2020.

Emaciated animals … for some it was too late
Tebogo
On the 23rd of February we received a call from an anonymous person who informed the SPCA that the animals at the Bloemfontein Zoo are dying because of hunger.
V/O
Bloemfontein SPCA inspector Tebogo Maswanganye and Senior Inspector Reinette Meyer rushed to the scene.
Reinette
Die Sondag toe ons hier kom was die buffels so honger gewees hulle het almal dadelik na ons toe aangestorm gekom. Ek het ‘n stukkie gras gevat buite en hulle met die hand gevoer en hulle het uit my hand uit geëet, so honger was hulle.

The Sunday when we came here these buffalo were so hungry they immediately stormed us. I picked a bit of grass from outside and fed them from my hand. They ate from my hand, that’s how hungry they were.
V/O
By the Sunday a buffalo and two Babary sheep had died. Most of the herbivores showed signs of severe malnutrition.
Reinette
Masa: And seeing them in that condition, what was going through your mind? How did that make you feel?

Reinette: Dit was eintlik een van die stegste dae in my lewe. Dit was terrible, dis nie lekker om dit te sien nie. Ons sien elke dag van ons lewe mishandeling en ons cope daarmee, maar hierdie is erg, dis te erg.

It was actually one of the worst days of my life. It was terrible. It is not nice to see this. We see animal abuse every day of our lives but we cope with it, but this is too severe, it’s too severe.
LINK
In December last year the provincial department of environmental affairs ordered the Mangaung Municipality to close the doors of the Bloemfontein zoo. This is after the municipality had issues around it’s permits.
V/O
While the Provincial Department of Economic, Small Business Development, Tourism and Environmental Affairs, or DESTEA, temporarily closed the zoo to visitors, the Mangaung Municipality was still responsible for the animals and the day-to-day running of the facility.


V/O
But the Mangaung Municipality has been buckling and systematically its services have become strained to the point where it’s been placed under administration. And during the two months away from the public eye, the Municipality did very little, it seems, to responsibly care for the animals housed at the zoo.


Tebogo
On that Sunday when we arrived here it was actually almost impossible for me to believe that animals can go without food under so many people. … And the first camp that we went to clearly indicated to me there is no food. It was very dry and there was really no sign of food at all. The way the animals came towards us and actually made a very strange sound.

It was really unbearable. Animals go on hunger to such an extent that they actually scream. … They were literally crying.


V/o
But not all the animals were screaming...
Reinette
Toe ons hier ingekom het op die 23ste Februarie, die voëls was doodstil. Ek het dit eintlik nog nooit in my lewe beleef nie. Voëls is praterige goed, hulle is chatty goed. Maar hierdie voëls was doodstil gewees.

When we came in here on the 23rd of February the birds were dead quiet. I have actually never experienced this in my life before. Birds are talkative things, they are chatty things. But these birds were dead quiet.
V/O
The aviary housed a selection of exotic and indigenous birds - amongst them South American Macaw and an endangered Cape Parrot.
Reinette
Wat ons hier gesien het was eintlik hartverskeurend gewees. Die voëls het bv die verkeerde soort kos geëet. Hulle het vir hulle mielies gegee. Nou parrots eet nie mielies nie, hulle het ‘n gebalanseerde dieëet nodig.

What we saw here was heart-wrenching. The birds ate the wrong type of food, for example. They gave them mealies. Parrots don’t eat mealies, they need a balanced diet.
V/O
Meyer and Maswanganye have been at loggerheads with the Municipality over the conditions at the zoo for some years, and their suspicions of long-term neglect were affirmed over and over...
Reinette
Kyk al die mis wat hierso lê -- Die probleem wat hier onstaan het, ons het hier kom inspeksies doen maar ons mag nooit in die enclosures ingekom het nie want dit is natuurlik ook te gevaarlik vir ons om in Wilde diere se enclosures in te gaan. Die werker wat hier moes skoonmaak het nooit skoongemaak nie alhoewel al die toerusting hier is.

Look at all the dung that lies here. The problem was that we came to do inspections but we were never allowed inside the enclosures because it is also dangerous for us to go into wild animals’ enclosures. So this happened. The worker that should have cleaned here never did even though the equipment is here.


Masa: How many zebras were here and how long would something like this take to accumulate?

Reinette: Hier het drie sebras gebly en hierdie sal maande vat. Dis nie net ‘n kwessie van ‘n dag of ‘n week nie. Dis maande, indien nie selfs jare, om dit so vuil te kry.

Three zebras lived here and this would take months. It’s not just a question of a day or a week. This takes months, if not years, to get it this dirty.
LINK
I remember visiting the zoo as a little girl, whether it would be through school excursions or with family, and those are some really fond and happy memories. Standing here today at the Bloemfontein zoo and seeing the appalling conditions the animals are meant to live in really is heartbreaking. The dirty water, the spider and cobwebs, and also the faeces, the general upkeep of this place clearly has been poor for a very long time.
V/O
Spokesperson for the Mangaung Municipality, Qondile Khedama has been evasive in his communication with Carte Blanche, so I decided to give him a call...
Qondile
Masa: Some of the animals had already died. So, we really would like to get some answers from the Municipality as to what went wrong here.

Khedama: Ja I wanted to … because senior, the intervention team that is currently in the municipality wanted to have an interaction with the provincial department… that is DESTEA… environments, and ja. So that is the thing that I thought that by now that meeting would have sat so that I’m actually having some information. But unfortunately there is nothing much that I can say.

Masa: You know Qondile, the SPCA came here last month already and to have no answers for this long…

Khedama: No it’s true, let me make an attempt again to meet with the intervention team.

Masa: I really hope that the Intervention Team does take it seriously because I must tell you Qondile, I’m sitting here inside the zoo and it really does not look good at all. The few animals that are left here… I feel for them. And to hear from your side as a municipality the steering committee and all these other meetings that are supposed to be taking place haven’t taken place in weeks already. It doesn’t leave a good taste in the mouth. You understand that right? It just leaves a sour taste, you understand?

Khedama: I, I, I… let me try to do my part. Then I’ll get back to you.

Masa: Alright, thank you very much Qondile, I appreciate that.


V/O
As the Mangaung Municipality is currently under administration, Khedama suggested we speak to Thomas Mkaza, a member of the Administrative team. But Mkaza did not respond to our emails or text messages.
V/O
The SPCA is adamant that the Mangaung Municipality will be held accountable.
Reinette
Masa: Reinette, are there going to be any consequences for the Mangaung Municipality?

Reinette: O, ja. Absoluut. Ons is besig om ons docket saam te stel en ons gaan ‘n klag van dieremishandeling lê teen al die betrokke partye - van die hoogste persoon in die munisipaliteit tot die laagste persoon. Almal wat betrokke was hierso gaan ons klagtes teen lê. Dit is absoluut moetswillig, dis onverantwoordelik en mense moet aan die pen ry vir daai dade.

Oh yes, absolutely. We are busy preparing a docket and will lay a charge of animal abuse against all parties involved - from the highest person in the municipality to the lowest person. Everyone involved here will be charged. This is absolutely willful, it is irresponsible and people have to account for their actions.
V/O
As it was clear that the animals could no longer remain under the custody of the municipality, the race was on to find new homes for the animals.
Hildegard
Lionsrock was asked if we would have the opportunity and the space for some of them. And we immediately also contacted all other sanctuaries we know.
V/O
All over South Africa, wildlife sanctuaries made arrangements to move the animals, all of it facilitated by the SPCA. Hildegard Pirker is the Head of Animal Welfare at Lionsrock Big Cat Sanctuary, established by FourPaws, and they’re taking the zoo’s two tigers and jackals. But every move comes with challenges.
Hildegard
The tigers are not even accessible at the moment, they are on the island and the moat is full with water and we cannot get there. So the fire brigade and some other organisations are helping us now to pump out the water because those animals couldn’t be accessible even if they need any other help than just throwing meat over. That is not really how you care in a zoo for animals, or in any place.
V/O
One by one the animals were carefully moved to NSPCA-approved locations. The big cats were screened for diseases, chipped and sent off to various sanctuaries.
LINK
The Bloemfontein Zoo used to house about 70 species. Most of the animals have been relocated to safe havens, except a few like the buffalo.
v/o
The Buffalo were first tested for TB and although they tested negative, they need to remain here for six months to be tested again before they can be moved.
Reinette
So hulle gaan vir ‘n geruime tyd nog hier staan. Maar ek will asseblief almal verseker. Ons kom hierheen, elke dag. Ons kom doen ons inspeksies, ons kom kyk dat hulle kos het. En as hier op ‘n stadium kom dat hier nie kos is nie sal ons defnitief aan hulle kos voorsien.

So they will remain here for some time, but we want to assure everyone we will come here every day. We’ll come do inspections and make sure they have food. If at some stage they do not have food we will definitely provide food.


V/O
For the SPCA inspectors, who have been fighting with the Municipality over conditions at the zoo for quite some time, there is a silver lining...
Reinette
Die een goeie punt, die een goeie ding waaroor ons kan bly wees … die diere is verwyder na baie goeie plekke toe. Ons kry gereeld videos nou van waar die diere is. Hulle is in beter omstandighede maar ons gaan bly seker maak dat alles goed gaan met hulle.

The one good thing, the one aspect for which we can be very glad… the animals have been moved to good places. We now regularly get videos of where the animals are. They are in better circumstances, but we’ll make sure that all is well with them.




PROMO 1 11”
Animals dying of hunger, - barren, dirty enclosures and over 70 species of animals that urgently needed new homes. We take a closer look at the collapse of the Bloemfontein zoo.




PROMO 2 11”
We investigate the appalling conditions at the Bloemfontein Zoo that led to the facility's permanent closure and the animals being confiscated from the care of the Mangaung Municipality.




PROMO 3 11”
UPSOUND - Ons sien elke dag van ons lewe mishandeling en ons cope daarmee, maar hierdie is erg, dis te erg.

What lead to the horrible death of some animals at the Bloemfontein zoo?

The worker that should have cleaned here never did even though the equipment is here. Masa: How many zebras were here and how long would something like this take to accumulate? Reinette: Hier het drie sebras gebly en hierdie sal maande vat. Dis nie net ‘n kwessie van ‘n dag of ‘n week nie. Dis maande, indien nie selfs jare, om dit so vuil te kry. Three zebras lived here and this would take months. It’s not just a question of a day or a week. This takes months, if not years, to get it this dirty. LINK I remember visiting the zoo as a little girl, whether it would be through school excursions or with family, and those are some really fond and happy memories. Standing here today at the Bloemfontein zoo and seeing the appalling conditions the animals are meant to live in really is heartbreaking. The dirty water, the spider and cobwebs, and also the faeces, the general upkeep of this place clearly has been poor for a very long time. V/O Spokesperson for the Mangaung Municipality, Qondile Khedama has been evasive in his communication with Carte Blanche, so I decided to give him a call... Qondile Masa: Some of the animals had already died. So, we really would like to get some answers from the Municipality as to what went wrong here. Khedama: Ja I wanted to … because senior, the intervention team that is currently in the municipality wanted to have an interaction with the provincial department… that is DESTEA… environments, and ja. So that is the thing that I thought that by now that meeting would have sat so that I’m actually having some information. But unfortunately there is nothing much that I can say. Masa: You know Qondile, the SPCA came here last month already and to have no answers for this long… Khedama: No it’s true, let me make an attempt again to meet with the intervention team. Masa: I really hope that the Intervention Team does take it seriously because I must tell you Qondile, I’m sitting here inside the zoo and it really does not look good at all. The few animals that are left here… I feel for them. And to hear from your side as a municipality the steering committee and all these other meetings that are supposed to be taking place haven’t taken place in weeks already. It doesn’t leave a good taste in the mouth. You understand that right? It just leaves a sour taste, you understand? Khedama: I, I, I… let me try to do my part. Then I’ll get back to you. Masa: Alright, thank you very much Qondile, I appreciate that. V/O As the Mangaung Municipality is currently under administration, Khedama suggested we speak to Thomas Mkaza, a member of the Administrative team. But Mkaza did not respond to our emails or text messages. V/O The SPCA is adamant that the Mangaung Municipality will be held accountable. Reinette Masa: Reinette, are there going to be any consequences for the Mangaung Municipality? Reinette: O, ja. Absoluut. Ons is besig om ons docket saam te stel en ons gaan ‘n klag van dieremishandeling lê teen al die betrokke partye - van die hoogste persoon in die munisipaliteit tot die laagste persoon. Almal wat betrokke was hierso gaan ons klagtes teen lê. Dit is absoluut moetswillig, dis onverantwoordelik en mense moet aan die pen ry vir daai dade. Oh yes, absolutely. We are busy preparing a docket and will lay a charge of animal abuse against all parties involved - from the highest person in the municipality to the lowest person. Everyone involved here will be charged. This is absolutely willful, it is irresponsible and people have to account for their actions. V/O As it was clear that the animals could no longer remain under the custody of the municipality, the race was on to find new homes for the animals. Hildegard Lionsrock was asked if we would have the opportunity and the space for some of them. And we immediately also contacted all other sanctuaries we know. V/O All over South Africa, wildlife sanctuaries made arrangements to move the animals, all of it facilitated by the SPCA. Hildegard Pirker is the Head of Animal Welfare at Lionsrock Big Cat Sanctuary, established by FourPaws, and they’re taking the zoo’s two tigers and jackals. But every move comes with challenges. Hildegard The tigers are not even accessible at the moment, they are on the island and the moat is full with water and we cannot get there. So the fire brigade and some other organisations are helping us now to pump out the water because those animals couldn’t be accessible even if they need any other help than just throwing meat over. That is not really how you care in a zoo for animals, or in any place. V/O One by one the animals were carefully moved to NSPCA-approved locations. The big cats were screened for diseases, chipped and sent off to various sanctuaries. LINK The Bloemfontein Zoo used to house about 70 species. Most of the animals have been relocated to safe havens, except a few like the buffalo. v/o The Buffalo were first tested for TB and although they tested negative, they need to remain here for six months to be tested again before they can be moved. Reinette So hulle gaan vir ‘n geruime tyd nog hier staan. Maar ek will asseblief almal verseker. Ons kom hierheen, elke dag. Ons kom doen ons inspeksies, ons kom kyk dat hulle kos het. En as hier op ‘n stadium kom dat hier nie kos is nie sal ons defnitief aan hulle kos voorsien. So they will remain here for some time, but we want to assure everyone we will come here every day. We’ll come do inspections and make sure they have food. If at some stage they do not have food we will definitely provide food. V/O For the SPCA inspectors, who have been fighting with the Municipality over conditions at the zoo for quite some time, there is a silver lining... Reinette Die een goeie punt, die een goeie ding waaroor ons kan bly wees … die diere is verwyder na baie goeie plekke toe. Ons kry gereeld videos nou van waar die diere is. Hulle is in beter omstandighede maar ons gaan bly seker maak dat alles goed gaan met hulle. The one good thing, the one aspect for which we can be very glad… the animals have been moved to good places. We now regularly get videos of where the animals are. They are in better circumstances, but we’ll make sure that all is well with them. PROMO 1 11” Animals dying of hunger, - barren, dirty enclosures and over 70 species of animals that urgently needed new homes. We take a closer look at the collapse of the Bloemfontein zoo. PROMO 2 11” We investigate the appalling conditions at the Bloemfontein Zoo that led to the facility's permanent closure and the animals being confiscated from the care of the Mangaung Municipality. PROMO 3 11” UPSOUND - Ons sien elke dag van ons lewe mishandeling en ons cope daarmee, maar hierdie is erg, dis te erg. What lead to the horrible death of some animals at the Bloemfontein zoo?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Animals at the Bloemfontein zoo left to die as the zoo's doors are closed.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In Feb/March 2019 Carte Blanche looked at the state of zoos around the country and the Bloemfontein Zoo was highlighted as an old fashioned zoo that provides very little educational value and poses a threat to the welfare of the animals. We saw barren, dirty enclosures where animals have very little stimulation and are surrounded by their own waste. Ponds and pools were dirty. The zoo was generally unkept. Then on 17 December 2019 the SPCA together with Free State Department: Economic, Small Business Development, Tourism and Environmental Affairs (DESTEA) closed the zoo down. The conditions had deteriorated to such an extent that the Manguang Municipality was ordered to move the animals and shut down the facility. The SPCA vowed to do regular inspections to check on the welfare of the animals. But by end Feb 2020 animals were dying from hunger and SPCA inspectors were greeted by a horrific scene.
metadata.Summary: The Manguang Municipality of Bloemfontein has been adamant that the city's zoo delivers a positive contribution to the community. In the beginning of 2019 they claimed to have adequate capacity in terms of people and funding to keep the zoo running without hiccups - even though there had been public outcries about the state of the animals in the past. By the end of 2019, the municipality admitted that they do not have the necessary resources to keep the facility running and DESTEA stepped in. The zoo was closed down, and the animals were to be relocated to other state facilities. But this never happened and by March 2020 animals were dying. At the moment animals are being moved to other facilities by DESTEA, but there is concern that because it is now an emergency, animals are sent to all kinds of facilities, even private farms where hunting is allowed. So the question is, will these state assets simply be discarded? There are also questions around the SPCA's conduct. On 7 Feb 2020 they issued a statement saying that the animals are fine.. Two weeks later animals are dying, buffalo are so sick that they're losing their hair, and many anilas are limping and listless. They were supposed to check regularly. What happened?
metadata.Further information: Manguang Municipality spokesperson Qondile Khedama acknowledged on Friday that there had been a myriad of issues at the zoo that the municipality had been working towards resolving. He said representatives had visited the zoo recently to assess the situation and condition of the animals. “Among other issues we have noted a serious lack of, or insufficient resources but an urgent meeting has since been called for an engagement with various stakeholders,” he said. The Bloemfontein Zoo has been in the news as early as 2012 about the conditions of enclosures and the state of animals. There are additional allegations that the property where the zoo is situated is earmarked for development and is part of an ongoing property war in the city.
